data.text:
Unfortunately, no exchange is completely immune from such incidents.

As for the threat to individuals  I completely agree.
Here’s a quick recap of recent events:

🇫🇷 Ledger Founder and Wife Kidnapped, Later Freed

On January 21, David Balland founder of the Ledger crypto wallet and his wife Amandine Balland were kidnapped from their home. They were forced into a car separated and held in different locations.

Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau stated that the kidnappers called Ledger’s leadership and demanded a large ransom in crypto. They reportedly mutilated Balland’s hand and sent a photo to Ledger to increase pressure.

Around 230 police officers were mobilized after Ledger alerted authorities. David was found on January 22 in Châteauroux, 30 miles southwest of his home. Amandine was found the next day after suspect interrogations and phone tracking in Étampes 80 miles away.

A small part of the ransom was paid, but it was frozen and traced, leading to nine men and one woman being arrested.

🇵🇭 Bitcoin Trader's Lambo Sale Turns into Kidnapping Attempt

On January 20, Korean BTC trader Taehwa Kim met with someone in Makati, Philippines who was supposedly interested in buying his Lamborghini.

After a test drive they stopped at a spa to "meet a lawyer." Three men forced Kim into another car and tied him up.
He was held for three days.

Eventually the attackers dumped him 50km away hands still bound where he was found by police.
While the attackers didn’t manage to steal his crypto, they took his car, Rolex, wallet, and apartment keys.

🇪🇸 $50M Crypto Ransom Demanded from Spanish Businessman

On March 29, São Paulo police arrested a former military officer in connection with the kidnapping of a Spanish businessman.

He was approached by two men dressed in fake police uniforms, thrown into a truck, and taken to a remote location where he was held captive and asked for $50 million in crypto.

Local media said the kidnappers drugged him, but he managed to escape while one of them used the restroom.
He found a gas station and alerted the police, who arrested a suspect and seized a gun and ammo.

🇫🇷 Kidnappers Targeted Father of Crypto Entrepreneur

On May 4, in Paris, the father of a French crypto entrepreneur was kidnapped.
He was taken 35 miles away to Essonne where his finger was cut off.
The kidnappers filmed it and sent the video to the entrepreneur, demanding €5 million in crypto.

The father was held for two days before being rescued.
CNN reported that five suspects were arrested.

🇫🇷 Daughter of Crypto Exchange Owner Escapes Abduction

The daughter and grandson of Pierre Noizat, CEO and co-founder of French crypto exchange Paymium, narrowly escaped a kidnapping attempt in Paris.
On May 13, three masked men tried to drag them into a van. Passersby intervened.

“In central Paris, a man was grabbed by hooded figures dressed in black. They attempted a kidnapping. A passerby with a fire extinguisher scared them off” reported Le Figaro.
The daughter managed to disarm one attacker and a nearby crowd stepped in.
The attackers fled and their van was later found abandoned.
Both victims were hospitalized for their injuries.

I want to remind you about an event that happened at the end of May

A recent data breach at the cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase raised serious concerns about user safety after hackers gained access to sensitive information, including home addresses.

On May 15 Coinbase  the third-largest crypto exchange in the world  confirmed that less than 1% of its monthly users were affected by the attack which could cost the company $400 million in reimbursements

However, the “human cost” of this data leak could be far greater for users according to Michael Arrington founder of TechCrunch and Arrington Capital

“Let me be clear: this hack  involving home addresses and account balances  will lead to people dying. It likely already has” Arrington said in a May 20 post on X @arrington

[3:49PM] #VictoriaIsland #TrafficUpdate 

Traffic on and around McWen bridge leading to and from Bonny Camp roundabout is currently flowing well. Similarly, Ahmadu Bello Way towards Eko Hotel and its return route are experiencing appreciable movement. 

The traffic flow from Bonny Camp underbridge through Kofo Abayomi, Oniru, Kilimajaro, down to Ozumba stretch and back is also in good condition, with the exception of brief holdups at traffic alternation areas.

 Furthermore, the route from Ozumba Avenue to Law School, connecting to Civic Center, BJ1004, School corner, and Sand Field heading inward Lekki Phase 1 and back, is moving steadily, again with slight delays at intersections.

data.text: TRAFFIC ADVISORY: Miramonte Blvd is closed between Kohl Street and Miramonte Court for a crash. Officers are investigating after vehicle hit a parked truck. That fire has since been put out. The road will be closed for at least another hour. Updates will be shared here. @NMFirePIO
